data.text/markdown:
Spike short: brainstorm board

What we trade. Liquid US stocks ($50+, ATR ≥ 3%, $100M+ daily dollar volume) that open 0.25–1.0 ATR up, then run another 4–5% before 10:00 ET. Short after the first red 1-minute bar, cover 20 minutes later. The problem. Most trades fade, but one or two a day keep running 2–5% and erase the winners. Stops tried so far cut winners as often as losers. Mark measures a small edge on 30-second bars and says it may be noise. What this group wants. Five to ten edges we can explain, test out of sample, and trade with our own money first. This page lists what has been tested, what failed, and what to try next, with a concrete example for each idea. Every number comes from a saved run; links point to the code and tools.

data.text/html:
1. Where we are

Alpaca SIP 1-minute bars, May 2025 – Nov 2026. Targets: win rate 60–70%, profit factor ≥ 1.5.

2. Ideas to test

Each has a concrete example and the test that would settle it.

3. Gap analysis (InfraNodus)

The call, Chris's brief, the emails and our results as a text network: strategy gap graph. The full news and gap analysis, with both graphs, answers from the graphs and the headline-by-outcome analysis, is in News and gap analysis (notebook 4). Clusters on either side of a gap are topics we discuss a lot but never connect. The biggest one: we talk about decision gates (vetoes, kill switches) and about timing (minutes after entry) but have no rule that uses the first minutes to make a gate decision with an explanation attached.Questions the gaps raise
  • Can a CLM-8B reranker that scores 8-K/10-K filings for fraud, delayed-financials or auditor-change language work as an entry-time veto that lifts tail-loser AUC above 0.57-0.7?
  • Can a millisecond veto, gated on the first red 1-minute bar and fed Form 4 / 8-K signals measured on 30-second bars, cut continuation-loser losses enough to lift profit factor above 1?
  • Can an explainable veto built from filing-derived narrative signals, tested on untouched sessions, show an edge that is testable rather than month-to-month noise?
Hypotheses that bridge them (rewritten as tests)
  • Participation decay: measure whether volume per minute after the arm falls off quickly (impatient buyers leaving, fade likely) or holds steady (a patient buyer still working an order, continuation likely). Exit on participation, not price.
  • Fill realism as a feature: the replay fills at the first print after the arm; a protected limit fills later or not at all. The fills a limit misses may be the trades that would have faded fastest, and the ones it gets may be the continuations.
  • Catalyst type sets the time scale: scheduled catalysts (earnings, guidance) attract buyers who work orders over hours; no-news spikes attract short-term traders. Tag each spike by catalyst type and compare continuation rates.

data.text/markdown:
6. What to build next (round 2)

# Work Why Output
1 Protected-limit entry in PyBroker Closest to how Chris actually trades; likely explains +164 vs +30 bps Fill rate, win rate, PF for tune / Q3 / Oct–Nov
2 Research loop round 2 Keep the heavy-red-bar skip and the early bail; drop the 10-minute rule; try ~10 ideas from section 2 Keep/undo ledger; holdout opened once at the end
3 Data-quality pass Gaps, splits and halts in cached bars can create fake tail losers List of trades that depend on bad bars
4 Async live prototype (src/live/) Alpaca websocket → screen → arm/entry state machine → paper-order stub, each with OpenTelemetry spans Pure decision functions ready to port to Rust
Tuning uses Jul 2025 – Jun 2026 only. Q3 2026 and Oct–Nov 2026 are opened once, at the end.

7. Tools

  • Jev Trading Lab: Where a millisecond decision model fits in the trade (13 levels)
  • Jev First-Hour Desk: Jev applied to the first trading hour
  • InfraNodus: Text-network gap analysis of notes, news and filings
  • CLM-8B: Embedding reranker for news or filing language
  • marimo: Reactive notebooks; the agent edits the same live session we look at
  • marimo Studio: Turns a notebook into a shareable page or slides
  • PyBroker: Independent backtester; reproduced the replay 136/136 trades
  • Alpaca market data: SIP 1-minute bars and news
  • Massive: Mark's data source: 30-second bars, long history
  • SEC EDGAR full-text search: Filing language before the headline
  • Lightweight Charts: Candles for bar-by-bar trade replay
  • OpenTelemetry: A trace span for each rule decision
